evidence.claim: The Bridges to Buttes Byway follows US 20 for 197 miles between the Wyoming border and Valentine.
evidence.quote: Bridges to Buttes Byway 197 miles from Valentine west to the Wyoming border on U.S. Highway 20.

evidence.claim: It is one of Nebraska’s designated scenic byways, a two-lane drive through bluffs, escarpments and the Sandhills.
evidence.quote: Along US-20, the route between the Wyoming state line and Valentine, a 197-mile (317 km) stretch, is designated the Bridges to Buttes Scenic Byway. Along this route, the highway passes through diverse landscapes such as escarpments and the Sandhills

evidence.claim: The Nebraska Tourism Commission emphasizes the change from rolling Sandhills in the east to prairie and pine-studded buttes toward the west.
evidence.quote: Scenery Rolling sandhills in the east, wild prairies in the northern Panhandle, and pine-studded buttes on the western edge.

evidence.quote: the U. S. Government authorized the establishment of a military camp at the agency site.

evidence.quote: Crazy Horse surrendered at the fort along with his 1,100 followers on May 6, 1877

evidence.claim: In January 1879, Northern Cheyenne prisoners broke out after the military withheld food, water and firewood to force their return to Indian Territory.
evidence.quote: Because the Cheyenne had refused to return to Indian Territory, on January 3rd, the military operating at Fort Robinson decided that they were going to withhold food, water and firewood

evidence.claim: U.S. soldiers pursued them, killing men, women and children.
evidence.quote: U.S. soldiers began hunting down the escapees, killing men, women, and children in the Fort Robinson massacre.

evidence.claim: Toadstool Geologic Park takes its name from rock formations shaped like toadstools.
evidence.quote: The park is named after its unusual rock formations, many of which resemble toadstools.

evidence.claim: North of Crawford in the Oglala National Grassland, it combines a badlands landscape with a reconstructed sod house.
evidence.quote: Toadstool Geologic Park is located in the Oglala National Grassland in far northwestern Nebraska. It is operated by the United States Forest Service. It contains a badlands landscape and a reconstructed sod house.

evidence.claim: A one-mile loop trail passes fossils. Remains of large prehistoric animals, including entelodonts and hyaenodons, have been found here.
evidence.quote: There is a 1-mile loop trail within the park. There are many fossils along the trail; removing fossils is not allowed. Many fossils of large prehistoric animals  such as entelodonts and hyaenodons have been found here.

evidence.claim: A separate three-mile Bison Trail leads toward Hudson-Meng Bison Kill, crossing Whitehead Creek and the ravine it forms between the park and the interpretive center.
evidence.quote: The Bison Trail to Hudson-Meng Bison Kill is a 3-mile hike. The route crosses Whitehead Creek, which forms a ravine splitting the plain between the geologic park and the kill bed interpretive center.

evidence.claim: Bryan Bridge was built in 1932 to carry US 20 over the Niobrara near Valentine.
evidence.quote: The Bryan Bridge was constructed to carry U.S. Route 20 over the Niobrara River in Cherry County, Nebraska, near Valentine.  It was built in 1932

evidence.claim: Its pin-connected cantilever arch was an engineering choice with an eye to the landscape.
evidence.quote: an excellent and well-preserved example of a pin-connected cantilever arch bridge.

evidence.claim: Designer Josef Sorkin told the National Register nominator that the design blended into its surroundings and was economical for the site.
evidence.quote: The NRHP nominator interviewed its designer, Josef Sorkin of the state's Division of Bridge Design, on why he chose this type of design, and reported that he replied "aesthetics, it blended into the surroundings and it was also an economical design for the site."

evidence.claim: The American Institute of Steel Construction selected it as the year’s most beautiful steel bridge in the category costing less than $250,000.

evidence.claim: US 20 now crosses the river north of the old bridge.
evidence.quote: U.S. Route 20 now crosses the Niobrara River about 2,000 feet (610 m) to the north.
